name: Fiss
kurzbeschreibung: Sunny high-altitude village featuring Tirol’s most family-friendly ski area and a Bikes-Arena.
beschreibung:
Overview

Fiss is perched at an elevation of 1,438 meters on the sun-drenched Serfaus-Fiss-Ladis plateau in the Tyrolean Oberland, within the district of Landeck. This historic alpine farming village, boasting over a millennium of documented history, rests approximately 500 meters above the Inn Valley floor and is home to roughly 1,050 residents. Despite evolving into one of the most celebrated family and outdoor destinations in the European Alps, Fiss has faithfully guarded its Rhaeto-Romanic village heritage, characterized by cobblestone lanes, robust stone farmsteads, and arched portals. Together with Serfaus and Ladis, the municipality creates an incomparable year-round alpine playground against the panorama of the Ötztal Alps.

History

Archaeological evidence confirms settlement on the plateau dating back to the Bronze and Iron Ages by Rhaetian tribes. Following the Roman conquest in 15 BC, indigenous and Roman cultures merged, fostering a distinct Rhaeto-Romanic language and architectural tradition that endured well into the late Middle Ages. The village name originates from the Latin term fossa, signifying a ditch or hollow, appearing in written records for the first time in 1286 as Füsse. The architectural identity of the town is shaped by massive masonry farmhouses with enclosed arched entryways. The parish church of Saint John the Baptist traces back to an early fourteenth-century chapel, consecrated in 1448 and later refurbished in baroque style. A globally unique cultural event is the Fisser Blochziehen carnival pageant, celebrated every four years in winter. Masked villagers pull a colossal 35-meter pine tree trunk symbolizing a giant plow through the streets to break winter's icy grip, inscribed as UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2011.

Getting There

By automobile, motorists take the Inntal motorway A12 and the S16 expressway to the Ried/Reschenpass exit, continuing along the B180 highway to Ried im Oberinntal. From Ried, the scenic L19 mountain road climbs via Ladis to Fiss in about fifteen minutes. To preserve alpine village serenity, the historic center is traffic-calmed, with ample designated parking at the cable car terminals near the entrance. Rail travelers arrive at the Landeck-Zams international railway hub, where direct Postbus line 214 departs regularly, reaching Fiss in about 45 minutes. A convenient local shuttle bus operates throughout the village.

Tips

In winter, the interconnected Serfaus-Fiss-Ladis ski arena offers 214 kilometers of immaculate slopes ascending to 2,828 meters at Masnerkopf, complemented by state-of-the-art lifts and Berta's Kinderland for young skiers. During summer, the Möseralm plateau transforms into the Summer Fun Park Fiss, featuring the thrilling Fisser Flieger kite glider soaring at 80 km/h, the Skyswing giant swing, and the 2.2-kilometer Fisser Flitzer toboggan coaster. Mountain bikers celebrate the premier Serfaus-Fiss-Ladis Bikepark and legendary singletrack descents like the Frommestrail. For peaceful relaxation, the scenic Wolfsee lake provides sun loungers and barefoot walking paths against sublime mountain backdrops.
metaDescription: Fiss on the Serfaus-Fiss-Ladis plateau: Renowned family ski arena, Möseralm summer fun park, Fisser Flieger glider and UNESCO Blochziehen heritage.
